'''Pavel Aleksandrovich Kulizhnikov''' ({{langx|ru|Павел Александрович Кулижников}}; born 20 April 1994) is a Russian [[Speed skating|speed skater]]. He won the [[2015 World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships – Men's 500 metres|men's 500 metres]] event at the [[2015 World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships|2015 World Single Distance Championships]] as well as the [[2015 World Sprint Speed Skating Championships|2015 World Sprint Championships]], becoming the youngest winner since speed skating icon [[Eric Heiden]] of the United States.<ref name=Worlds2015/> In 2015, he became the first speed skater to finish the 500-meter in under 34 seconds with a [[World record progression 500 m speed skating men|world record]] of 33.98.<ref name=wr>{{cite web|url= http://www.speedskatingresults.com/index.php?p=9|title= World Records|publisher = speedskatingresults.com|access-date = 14 February 2022}}</ref> In 2020 he became the first speed skater to break 1:06 in the 1000 metres. At the [[2016 World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships|2016 World Single Distance Championships]], Kulizhnikov won the men's 500 m and 1000 m, becoming the first man to win gold in both distances at the same speed skating World Single Distances Championships.<ref name=Worlds2016/>

==Career==
===Junior===
Kulizhnikov was a talented junior and prodigy, winning numerous of the Junior World Cup in the 2010–2011 and 2011–2012 seasons. At the [[2012 World Junior Speed Skating Championships|2012 World Junior Championships]] in [[Obihiro]], Japan, then 17-year-old Kulizhnikov won gold in the 1000 meters and bronze in the 500 meters, but was later disqualified for a doping violation, with his results annulled, and suspended for two years ending his quest to compete at the [[2014 Winter Olympics|2014 Sochi Olympics]]. Kulizhnikov stated that [[methylhexanamine]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Magnar Taule|url=http://sport.bt.no/sport/skoyter/article262641.ece|title=Fikk VM-gull i posten etter russisk juks|publisher=Bergens Tidende / BT.no|date=3 January 2013|access-date=8 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106080258/http://sport.bt.no/sport/skoyter/article262641.ece|archive-date=6 January 2013|quote=Men så – utpå høsten i fjor – ble det kjent at Pavel Kulizjnikov hadde testet positivt på kroppsbyggerdopet methylhexamine. Russeren ble dermed fratatt gullet, og Lorentzen ble flyttet opp fra sølv- til gullplass.}}</ref> was found in his body because of a nasal spray for colds.

===Senior===
====2014–15====
After a two-year doping suspension, Kulizhnikov debuted in his first [[2014–15 ISU Speed Skating World Cup|World Cup series]] in 2014–2015; he started his competition in [[Obihiro]] by taking gold in 1000 meters and silver in 500 meters.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.sportnavigator.nl/nws/2014/11/kulizhnikov-big-surprise-of-first-isu-world-cup.html|title= Kulizhnikov big surprise of first ISU World Cup|access-date= 17 November 2014|publisher= Sportnavigator|url-status= dead}}</ref> He won a total of 3 gold at the [[2014–15 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – Men's 1000 metres|2014–15 World Cup men's 1000 meters]] and 8 gold in [[2014–15 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – Men's 500 metres|2014–15 World Cup men's 500 metres]]. He won gold at the [[2015 World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships|2015 World Single Distance Championships]] in 500 meters,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20150208/spd--speedskating-world-cup/|title=Pavel Kulizhnikov wins World Cup speedskating 500 meters|date=8 February 2015|access-date= 1 March 2015|work= [[HuffPost]]}}</ref> as well as the [[2015 World Sprint Speed Skating Championships|2015 World Sprint Championships]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.isu.org/en/speed-skating/news/2015/03/isu-world-sprint-speed-skating-champs-astana-kaz-day-2|title=Bowe and Kulizhnikov clinch World Sprint title in style|access-date=1 March 2015|publisher=ISU|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326052331/http://www.isu.org/en/speed-skating/news/2015/03/isu-world-sprint-speed-skating-champs-astana-kaz-day-2|archive-date=26 March 2015}}</ref> 18 years later since the last Russian [[Sergey Klevchenya]] won Sprint. He is also the youngest speed skater to win since speed skating Icon [[Eric Heiden]] of the United States.<ref name=Worlds2015/> Kulizhnikov withdrew from the last leg of the World Cup series of the season nursing a back injury, his teammate [[Ruslan Murashov]] won the final event of the series in 500 meters in [[Erfurt]], Germany. Kulizhnikov took 1st place in the overall ranking in the men's speed skating for 500 m and 1000 m in the 2014–15 World Cup Series. He underwent back treatment in the first half of the season.

====2015–16====
For the 2015–16 season, Kulizhnikov competed at the [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – Men's 500 metres|2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup]] in [[Calgary]], winning the 500 m with a new Russian record of 34.11. He then won silver in [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – Men's 1000 metres|1000 m]], updating his record to 1:07.33. On 15 November 2015, Kulizhnikov broke the [[World record progression 500 m speed skating men|world record]] in men's 500 m, clocking a time of 34.00 seconds to beat the previous record of 34.03 set by [[Jeremy Wotherspoon]] of Canada in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://citizen.co.za/afp_feed_article/russias-kulizhnikov-american-bowe-set-speed-skating-world-records/|title= Russia's Kulizhnikov set speed skating world records|access-date= 15 November 2015|publisher= Citizen|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151117015411/http://citizen.co.za/afp_feed_article/russias-kulizhnikov-american-bowe-set-speed-skating-world-records/|archive-date= 17 November 2015}}</ref> Five days later at the second [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – World Cup 2|World Cup]] meet in [[Salt Lake City]] on 20 November 2015, he improved his world record to 33.98.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/2812a787795e46aea85a9045065e9051/russias-kulizhnikov-breaks-world-500-record-again|title=Russia's Kulizhnikov breaks world 500 record again |access-date= 20 November 2015|agency= Associated Press}}</ref> He then won the men's 1000 m with an updated personal best of 1:06.70. Kuliznikov withdrew from the list in competition at the [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – World Cup 3|2015–16 ISU World Cup]] in [[Inzell]] because of the flu.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://m.schaatsupdate.nl/schaatsnieuws/4791/kulizhnikov-laat-alle-wedstrijden-in-inzell-schieten/|title= Kulizhnikov laat alle wedstrijden in Inzell schieten|access-date= 5 December 2015|publisher= schaatsupdate.nl|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151222083354/http://m.schaatsupdate.nl/schaatsnieuws/4791/kulizhnikov-laat-alle-wedstrijden-in-inzell-schieten/|archive-date= 22 December 2015}}</ref>

He returned to competition at the [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – World Cup 4|2015–16 World Cup]] in [[Heerenveen]], where he won gold medals in 500 m and 1000 m in a time of 1:08.16 (a track record, and a lowland world record).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eurosport.co.uk/speed-skating/kulizhnikov-at-record-pace-in-heerenveen_sto5026264/story.shtml|title=Kulizhnikov at record pace in Heerenveen |access-date= 11 December 2015|publisher= Eurosport}}</ref> On the third day of competition in 500 m race, Kulizhnikov unexpectedly fell in the inner corner in his mid-race and finished 20th, teammate [[Ruslan Murashov]] won the event. Kulizhnikov was unharmed from the fall and did not suffer any major injuries.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://schaatsupdate.nl/schaatsnieuws/4846/kulizhnikov-onderuit-op-tweede-omloop-murashov-profiteert/|title= Kulizhnikov onderuit op tweede omloop, Murashov profiteert|access-date= 13 December 2015|publisher= schaatsupdate.nl|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151222164736/http://www.schaatsupdate.nl/schaatsnieuws/4846/kulizhnikov-onderuit-op-tweede-omloop-murashov-profiteert/|archive-date= 22 December 2015}}</ref> In 29–31 January, Kulizhnikov competed at the [[2015–16 ISU Speed Skating World Cup – World Cup 5|ISU World Cup in Stavanger]] winning the gold medals in 500 m and in 1000 m, where he updated his new [[List of world records in speed skating|Lowland world record]] time of 1:08.10.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.schaatsstatistieken.nl/index.php?file=records&g=m&type=laag|title=World Records |access-date= 30 January 2016|publisher= schaatsupdate.nl}}</ref> On 11–14 February, at the [[2016 World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships]] in [[Kolomna]], Kulizhnikov won two gold medals, winning the men's 500 m and 1000 m,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tass.ru/en/sport/856675|title=Kulizhnikov wins 500m world title at World Single Distance Speed Skating Championships |access-date= 14 February 2016|agency= Information Telegraph Agency of Russia}}</ref> becoming the first man to win gold in both distances at the same speed skating World Single Distances Championships.<ref name=Worlds2016/> In 26–28 February, Kulizhnikov retained his Sprint title winning the [[2016 World Sprint Speed Skating Championships]] held in [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]].<ref name=Sprint2016/>

=====Meldonium case=====
On 8 March 2016, it was reported that Kulizhnikov had failed a drug test, testing positive for [[meldonium]], an [[Ischemia|anti-ischemic]] drug added to the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] (WADA)'s banned substances list in 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Russian speed skater Pavel Kulizhnikov has failed meldonium test, says coach|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/mar/08/russian-speedskater-tests-positive-meldonium|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=8 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author1=Lidia Kelly|title=Meldonium detected in Russian speed skaters Elistratov and Kulizhnikov – R-sport|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-sharapova-russia-skaters-idUSKCN0WA1JP|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=8 March 2016}}</ref> On 13 April, the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] gave amnesty to athletes with the presence of less than one microgram of meldonium in blood. Doping samples in tests conducted on athletes before 1 March 2016 with abnormal levels of the drug are acceptable, WADA cited due to uncertainties and lack of studies for how long meldoniumnstays in the body.<ref>{{cite news|author1=Dmitriy Rogovitskiy|title=Doping-WADA announces meldonium amnesty|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/doping-wada-meldonium-idUKL3N17G2SK|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160416143221/http://uk.reuters.com/article/doping-wada-meldonium-idUKL3N17G2SK|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2016|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=13 April 2016}}</ref> On 21 April 2016, the [[International Skating Union]] lifted its temporary ban on Kulizhnikov, and he was reinstated in the team since the concentration of meldonium was below the threshold.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ria.ru/sport/20160421/1416544010.html|title=Амнистия по полной: ISU снял обвинения в допинге c трех конькобежцев|date=21 April 2016|agency=RIA Novosti|language=ru|access-date=21 April 2016}}</ref>

The International Skating Union's Official Statement was quoted: "In the case of Meldonium, the WADA recognized that there is currently a lack of clear scientific information on excretion time and considers that in certain circumstances there may be grounds for no fault or negligence on the part of the athlete.
All mentioned skaters credibly assured the ISU that they had discontinued the use of Meldonium before 1 January 2016, when the substance was included in the prohibited list. In light of the given information, the ISU has decided to lift the provisional suspension imposed on the four skaters, with immediate effect, to stay the results management process and consequently not to disqualify any results at the present stage."<ref name=ISU16/>

====2019–20====
In the [[2019–20 ISU Speed Skating World Cup|2019–20 World Cup season]], Kulizhnikov missed out on the first two stages due to an injury received during practice. He then skipped the following stage in [[Nur-Sultan]]. He returned to the ice rink in [[Nagano (city)|Nagano]], collecting four medals, two of which were gold ones: in the 1000 m and, for the first time, in the team sprint. In the 1000 m event, he set a track record.<ref>[https://live.isuresults.eu/events/2020_JPN_0001/competition/23/results ISU World Cup #4 – 1000m Men Division A]</ref> In the following [[Calgary]] stage, he set another track record in the same event.<ref>[https://live.isuresults.eu/events/2020_CAN_0001/competition/12/results ISU World Cup #5 – 1000m Men Division A]</ref>

Kulizhnikov entered the [[2020 World Single Distances Speed Skating Championships|2020 World Single Distances Championships]], taking place at [[Utah Olympic Oval]] in [[Salt Lake City]]. During the [[2020 World Single Distances Speed Skating Championships – Men's team sprint|team sprint]] event, Kulizhnikov tumbled, so his team did not finish the run. The fall resulted in Kulizhnikov having his shoulders dislocated.<ref>[https://www.isu.org/media-centre/press-releases/2020-6/23807-isu-world-single-distances-speed-skating-championships-salt-lake-city-usa-day-two/file Men’s 500m: Kulizhnikov defies shoulder problem to take gold]</ref> However, the Russian took part in the [[2020 World Single Distances Speed Skating Championships – Men's 500 metres|500 m]] distance and achieved victory. After the 500 m, he planned to skip the [[2020 World Single Distances Speed Skating Championships – Men's 1000 metres|1000 m]] event.<ref>[https://www.championat.com/other/news-3972887-kulizhnikov-hotel-snjatsja-s-distancii-na-1000-m-no-v-itoge-pobil-mirovoj-rekord.html Кулижников: хотел сняться с дистанции на 1000 м, но в итоге побил мировой рекорд]</ref> Despite that, Kulizhnikov was persuaded not to do that; as a result, he finished the 1000 m event with a [[World record progression 1000 m speed skating men|new world record]] (1:05.69).<ref>[https://www.isu.org/media-centre/press-releases/2020-6/23809-isu-world-single-distances-speed-skating-championships-salt-lake-city-usa-day-three/file Men’s 1000m: Calm Kulizhnikov can’t be topped]</ref> Kulizhnikov held the world record for just under four years before [[Jordan Stolz]] lowered it on 26 January 2024, also in Salt Lake City.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/olympics/news/jordan-stolz-world-record-1000-meters-speed-skating|title=Jordan Stolz breaks 1000m speed skating world record|author=OlympicTalk|website=[[NBC Sports]]|publisher=[[NBCUniversal]]|date=27 January 2024|access-date=29 January 2024}}</ref>

===Achievements===
* Second-youngest world champion since [[Eric Heiden]] of the United States.<ref name=Worlds2015/>
* First male speed skater to win 500m and 1000m gold at the same speed skating World Single Distances Championships.<ref name=Worlds2016/>
